items.title: M-A-S-K
items.decryption: Reminds you that the Kandahar bilingual inscription uses Greek and Aramaic scripts, distinct from Brahmi/Kharosthi used elsewhere.

items: Confusing the Kandahar Bilingual Edict (Greek/Aramaic) with standard Brahmi inscriptions.
Assuming all edicts mention 'Ashoka' by name; many refer to him as 'Devanampiya Piyadassi'.
Believing inscriptions are only in India; they exist in modern-day Afghanistan and Pakistan.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Northern: Shahbazgarhi, Mansehra
  • Southern: Brahmagiri, Maski
  • Western: Girnar, Sopara
  • Eastern: Dhauli, Jaugada

Personalities

  • Devanampiya: Beloved of Gods
  • Piyadassi: Pleasant to behold
  • James Prinsep: Deciphered Brahmi (1837)

Classification of Edicts

  • Major Rock Edicts (14)
  • Minor Rock Edicts
  • Major Pillar Edicts
  • Cave Inscriptions (Barabar Hills)
ScriptRegion
BrahmiMost of India
KharosthiNorth-West Frontier (Pak)
AramaicAfghanistan
GreekKandahar
